about: Speaking in five (25 Nov 2026): the Writing 'in five' ladder for a Speaking Part, in the school's blueprint: the moves and labels of Practise (the Tomás and Beatriz models), three alternative chunks per move, the Part's Practise topics. {X} = what the pupil picks. 'q' is the examiner's question.
name: Part 2
how: A Part 2 minute in five: what the photos share, how they differ, a guess that compares them, develop it, then the question answered. Same five, any photos.

nameAsk.title: What do both photos show?
nameAsk.aim: Pick how you'd say it. Your first sentence will use it.

subjects.label: Work
subjects.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be difficult for the people in these situations.
subjects.scene: Photo 1: a team in a meeting · Photo 2: someone working alone in a café

subjects.label: Social
subjects.q: Compare the two photographs and say how the people might be feeling in these situations.
subjects.scene: Photo 1: a crowded street at night · Photo 2: students working in a library

subjects.label: Entertainment
subjects.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have chosen to spend their time in these ways.
subjects.scene: Photo 1: people at the cinema · Photo 2: a family playing a board game

subjects.label: Shopping
subjects.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be enjoyable or frustrating about shopping in these places.
subjects.scene: Photo 1: a big shopping centre · Photo 2: a traditional market

subjects.label: Outdoor
subjects.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have decided to spend their time in these ways.
subjects.scene: Photo 1: a beach at sunset · Photo 2: someone hiking in the mountains

subjects.label: Learning
subjects.q: Compare the two photographs and say what the people might be learning from these experiences.
subjects.scene: Photo 1: students in a library · Photo 2: a parent helping children with a tablet

subjects.label: Sports
subjects.q: Compare the two photographs and say what skills the people might be developing through these activities.
subjects.scene: Photo 1: a football team · Photo 2: someone training alone in a gym

subjects.label: Travel
subjects.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might make these travel experiences memorable for the people.
subjects.scene: Photo 1: tourists in a city · Photo 2: an adventure by a mountain lake

slots.label: Similar
slots.job: open with what both photos share
slots.q: Which one says what the photos share?

ways.t: What both photos have in common is {X}.
In both cases, I can see {X}.

slots.label: Different
slots.job: say how the photos differ, in one sentence

ways.t: Whereas the first photo shows …, the second one shows …
In the first photo …, but in the second photo …
The first photo shows …, while the second …

slots.label: Guess
slots.job: guess, comparing the people, with evidence
slots.q: Which one makes a guess that compares?

ways.t: Judging by their faces, the people in the first photo might be more … than …
From the way they're standing, they look as if …
The people in the second photo are probably …

slots.label: Develop
slots.job: develop your guess: a reason OR an example

slots.label: Answer
slots.job: answer the question printed above the photos
slots.q: Which one answers the question on the page?

ways.t: Overall, I think the second situation is more … , although …
To answer the question, I think …
